study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting task-based fMRI activity using normative modelling: an application to the Emotional Face Matching Task

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Bayesian Linear Regression (Gaussian BLR); warped BLR compared but not used for main results.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: by training a Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) model to predict BOLD signal for the faces>shapes contrast. In preliminary analyses, we compared a warped model which can model nonGaussianity with a vanilla Gaussian BLR model. Since the fit was comparable across most metrics and regions, we focus on the simpler Gaussian model below.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Task-evoked BOLD activation z-statistic maps for faces>shapes and faces>baseline contrasts.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The z-statistic maps from the contrast face>shapes (contrast vector [1, -1]; 5 mm smoothed in standard space), for each subject, were used as response variables for the normative models. We also created models to predict BOLD signal for the faces condition alone (i.e. face>baseline contrast vector [1, 0]).

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Predictors included site, age, sex, intra-cranial volume, acquisition parameters (TR, multiband sequence), counts (number of volumes collected; number of target blocks), and task parameters (task length, instructions, target stimuli).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We created normative models of EFMT-related BOLD activation maps, as a function of site, age, sex, intra-cranial volume, and acquisition [TR, multiband sequence, number of volumes collected (per run where applicable)] and task parameters [task length (in seconds, and per run where applicable), number of target blocks, instructions for faces condition, and the target stimuli (i.e. which stimulus set they came from)].
